qa_pairs.question: What is the tuition refund percentage for a course dropped during standard add/drop versus between add/drop and the census date?

qa_pairs.question: What are the conditions and default deadline for receiving an Incomplete ('I') grade?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An incomplete grade requires at least 70% of assessed work complete and passing status before an unexpected documented event. The student and instructor sign a plan, and the default deadline is the end of the next regular term, after which it converts to F if uncompleted.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently.
The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.
Neither office changes grades or waives essential programme outcomes.

qa_pairs.question: How does an approved medical leave differ from a voluntary leave regarding scholarship protection and tuition credit?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms without using the probation term, and may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study. Voluntary leave does not automatically reserve the award unless deferral is requested before census.

contexts.text: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity.
A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms.
An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation.
